messages.subject: emacs mode (not yet finished, but in the repository)
parts:
It's not finished, but the start is in src/StanMode/stan-mode.el. If
anyone wants me to move it, please let me know.

Some details:
- implemented as a derived mode. Parent mode is cc-mode
- currently highlights:
* blocks
* Stan keywords
* functions
* distributions (picks up "<- foo_log()" and "~ foo()", but won't
highlight both)
* comments
- indents when comments are "//" and not "#"

Items left to finish:
- I forgot to highlight truncations: "T"
- Stan menu
* Need to remove C++ menu
* Need to add Stan menu. I'm thinking: Comment Region, Uncomment
Region, Indent Line or Region
- Indentation:
* We can discuss style, but C++ seems to work out fine.
* Can't parse '#' as comments: cc-mode defines indentation.
Currently picking out '#' as a preprocessor declaration, but we've
hijacked that symbol for a comment in the syntax-map. I was looking
through the cc-mode lisp code for indentation, but there wasn't a
clear way to make the indentation use '#' and not treat it as a
comment. Two options: 1) get more familiar with cc-mode's indentation
or 2) write own indent code.

Just in case anyone wants to try it out, add these two lines to .emacs
or preferences (aquamacs: ~/Library/Preferences/Aquamacs
Emacs/Preferences.el):

(add-to-list 'load-path "<STAN-HOME>/src/StanMode/")
(require 'stan-mode)





Daniel

Jeff,

On Thu, Nov 1, 2012 at 12:02 PM, Jeffrey Arnold <jeffrey...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Daniel, 

I know have a little bit of time to devote to stan-mode. 

Where do you want to host stan-mode?  I've looked at your code. I can merge most of what you did into my mode pretty easily. 

Good question. I wouldn't mind keeping it with Stan (the Stan google repository). That, of course, means that we'd be committing to it for a while. With merging, yes, I agree. It looks like we were doing very similar things. Are you ok with the licensing we chose for Stan? We could distribute Stan mode under a different license if that makes more sense.
 
The main difference is whether to derive the mode from fundamental or c-mode. I recall trying c-mode, because
I didn't want to reinvent the wheel. But I found the indentation code both too customizable and too strict, and got tied up on how to get 
it to accept # as indentation. I could revisit it.  I know that one of the javascript modes does hacks c-mode indentation to get it to work correctly.  I abandoned trying to derive from c-mode, believing it was better to have no indentation than bad indentation. The indentation rules (ignoring comments) seem pretty straightforward. This is what I inferred from the manual.



  • Lines ending with ; are complete statements/expr
  • Default indentation width = 2
    • 

  • If complete statement, indent at same level as previous complete statement
    • 

  • If not complete statement, then indent to
    • open ( or [
    • 
<-, ~ 
    • last line + indent
  • If previous line ends in {, indent >>
    • 

  • If previous line ends in }, indent <<
  • If previous line begins with "for", indent >>

I definitely feel you. I was able to get '#' recognized by switching the character in the syntax table to a comment. That fixed the indentation.

In Aquamacs (mac port of emacs), the syntax table doesn't work perfectly, so I wanted to change '/*' and '*/' back to normal characters and just pick up highlighting on my own. Bob found out that the transpose operator (single quote) messes up indentation. I think it's as simple as switching the single quote character in the syntax table.

The BNF grammar is in the manual and Bob has been very good about keeping it up to date. That'll help us out.

If you wanted to build indentation rules from scratch, that's fine by me. With regards to indentation rules, we might be able to write a reasonable guide and enforce it with something like a Stan mode.
My plan of attack was to try to implement indenting with SMIE or semantic first, and if that didn't work just write custom function.

My next TODOs
  • indentation: trying in order: SMIE, semantic, c-mode, and then custom functions.
  • highlight blocks 
  • yasnippet snippets for all functions 
  • menu interface
Looks good to me.


Long run, do you want to include stan-mode in ess?  

I wasn't thinking that far ahead, but sounds reasonable, as long as it's not too much of a pain. If it is a pain, I'm more than happy not having it in ess. As of right now, both our modes are really lightweight and don't depend on much.

 

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] emacs mode (not yet finished, but in the repository)
parts: Good question. I wouldn't mind keeping it with Stan (the Stan google repository). That, of course, means that we'd be committing to it for a while. With merging, yes, I agree. It looks like we were doing very similar things. Are you ok with the licensing we chose for Stan? We could distribute Stan mode under a different license if that makes more sense.

I'm fine with including it as part of official Stan; that seems to make the most sense.  I think the license for the emacs mode should be GPL. It's not that I have a strong preference for that, but it appears that almost every emacs library that I've seen is licensed under the GPL.   

Now my version of the mode is derived from c++-mode, and I've merged in all functionality that was in your mode and missing from mine.   I got the indentation for # to work by defining a new style that redefines the indentation for cpp-macro. Now stan-mode has support for font-lock, indentation, imenu, and compiler-mode.  I also wrote two small libraries to add support for yasnippets and flymake.

To make it easier to install, I added a recipe for MELPA (https://github.com/jrnold/melpa/blob/master/recipes/stan-mode). I'll put in a pull request to the official melpa repo whenever the stan-mode integration into the official stan repo is done.

Let me know how you want to proceed.

Jeff
